# Behavioral Neuroscience 392: course-specific lecture rules

These instructions apply ONLY to this course. The instructor’s request takes precedence over inherited Neuroethology rules. This is the connected BEHAVNEUR-392- GitHub repository at https://github.com/jordanxxlopez/BEHAVNEUR-392-.git. Keep all Behavioral Neuroscience materials in this repository, separate from NEUR 411.

## Deliverables and level

Build 19 chapter PowerPoints, one per verified chapter in Carlson and Birkett, Physiology of Behavior, Global Edition, 13th edition (2022), ISBN 9781292430256. Verify the table of contents before recording chapter mapping. The instructor explicitly requests descriptive lecture titles, not "Chapter 1"; use the authorized topic title in course/schedule.json. Start with Chapter 1 unless directed otherwise. Prefer 75 slides total: 1 title, 73 content, 1 final Key takeaways. Expand only when useful, to at most 85 total. Do not invent a timetable. Each chapter may span several class meetings.

This is an undergraduate Behavioral Neuroscience course, easier than NEUR 411 but intellectually demanding. Define terms at first use. Explain neuronal signaling, pathways, experimental manipulations, and behavioral findings through direct, concrete teaching sentences. Introduce unfamiliar machinery in steps; avoid graduate-level prerequisite knowledge.

## Teaching and balance

Use 30–40% textbook foundations and 60–70% primary-research teaching, adjusted to the chapter. At the preferred count, 29 foundation slides and 44 research slides give approximately 40%/60%. Foundation slides teach mechanisms from the textbook even when an existing study figure illustrates the concept; retagging alone is insufficient. Tag each content slide instructional_role as foundation or research; do not count an incidental citation as research teaching. The textbook defines chapter scope and concepts. Interweave concept teaching with directly related primary studies rather than separating a foundation block from a research block. Connect studies to the topic and mechanism just introduced; emphasize current research while revisiting essential older work. Never say "the textbook" or add textbook metacommentary in visible teaching prose. References and source-image credits still identify the textbook accurately. Review every video and added image for its relationship to the adjacent concept, not merely its availability. Teach each concept, then use source-supported study findings to explain how it works. Use a manageable group of core papers across several slides rather than a different paper on every slide. Include current accessible research and foundational work where needed; verify references and quantitative claims.

Every paragraph teaches material. Use direct, concrete teaching sentences in three paragraphs. Each content paragraph must occupy 5–7 full rendered lines, checked against the exported PDF. Expand explanations rather than add filler, forced line breaks, or blank-line padding. The line requirement supersedes the earlier 70–110-word target. Identify the actor, action, and result. Do not summarize with vague verbs such as connected, linked, supported, or relationship. For example: "The neurons move the paddle. A hit or miss determines the electrical signal sent back to them." Scientific connections can still be described literally when their anatomy is the subject. Use three substantive paragraphs per content slide and natural complete-sentence teaching transcripts in notes, adapting depth to this easier class and readable layout. Do not pad paragraphs to meet a sentence count. No agendas, learning objectives, previews, fixed method-result-limitation templates, presentation commentary, or em dashes in visible text. Do not end paragraphs on routine limitations or stock caution. The instructor will discuss limitations and the importance of controls orally. Preserve scientifically necessary distinctions and genuine experimental conditions; do not turn hypotheses into facts. No p-values, error bars quoted in prose, test names, or sample-size bookkeeping. Retain quantities that explain the concept. Finish with 5–6 exam-level takeaways with bold lead phrases.

## Format

16:9, Arial throughout. Preserve the Neuroethology content-slide style. For this course’s TITLE SLIDE ONLY: white background, a large credited source image on the LEFT, and the instructor-approved descriptive lecture title, course/date, Jordan Lopez, Ph.D., and Professor of Neurobiology & Biomedical Engineering on the RIGHT. Do not mirror or recolor the source image. Body text/captions/footers black; titles and bold words use the chapter’s coordinated restrained theme. Separate theme ledger from NEUR 411; no yellow, orange, gold, purple, or green. Record themes after final validation. Never copy the former professor’s slide style. Analyze their slides for existing course coverage only when available.

## Figures

Every content slide has a relevant source image. Preserve existing intact study panels. Add a few original credited cell, anatomy, animal, or apparatus photographs where these make the slide concept recognizable. Fit images and movies without changing source aspect ratios or making scientific panels illegible. Prioritize intact primary-article panels. Textbook crops are explicitly allowed for foundations: retain original labels, caption Carlson and Birkett (2022), figure number and printed page, and record PDF page, ISBN, edition, and source. Retain enough context for students to interpret axes, labels, units, and scale bars. Never generate, redraw, replot, recolor, or reconstruct any scientific image, diagram, chart, or animation. Up to 10 genuinely useful credited web images are permitted. Give the full source reference in notes. New crops are made with tools/crop_figure.py; record crop boxes. Do not post the full uploaded textbook to GitHub.

## Videos

For Chapter 2 and subsequent new chapter decks, require exactly 20 distinct useful academic videos PLUS 20 distinct aesthetic animal/neuroscience recordings, totaling 40 embedded videos. This instructor update supersedes the former 20–30-video range. Existing Chapter 1 deliveries retain their recorded media counts unless a revision is requested. Choose each recording for its adjacent concept; do not reuse unrelated repository footage merely because it is available. For Chapter 3 onward, distribute all 40 recordings across the entire content sequence: 10 in each consecutive quarter, no gap greater than three content slides, and at least five in the final ten content slides. Never put media-purpose labels such as aesthetic, academic recording, or context video in visible slide text, captions, titles, or teaching notes. Keep these classifications only in the media manifest. Spread them through the material where appropriate; preserve article figures on video slides. Academic web/YouTube recordings by primary researchers and labs are permitted even when not publisher supplementary movies. No news reports, shorts, TikTok-style edits, unrelated entertainment, or fabricated scenes. Verify and accurately credit source authors, original URLs, study DOI when associated, and supplied license. Aesthetic recordings are real footage connected to the chapter, credited, with their purpose classified in internal records only, and never counted as primary scientific evidence or toward the academic-video quota. User uploads remain uploads, not fabricated article supplements.

Embed PowerPoint-compatible MP4s. Preserve native resolution, timing, audio, aspect ratio, and scientific scenes. Compress only when necessary and verify quality. Record video purpose (academic/aesthetic), slide, source, DOI if applicable, dimensions, duration, audio, codec, and SHA256. Verify every embedded media relationship and all source hashes; do not count duplicate excerpts as different studies or pad with repetitions. Retain static source posters. Report untested desktop playback honestly.

# Teaching prose and speaker transcripts

This instructor correction applies to all Behavioral Neuroscience chapters and authorized revisions. It applies equally to visible slide text and the teaching transcript before References in speaker notes. Source credits and original figure legends retain their source wording.

Teach the mechanism, anatomy, physiology, and behavior directly, at the plain-language level of the instructor's supplied cannabinoid rewrite below. Use connected explanations, definitions woven into the prose, and clear descriptions of what changes in the cell. A slide should leave the student able to explain a specific biological process, not merely repeat that a study examined it. Do not replace vague prose with a dense list of technical proteins or experimental abbreviations.

- Name the actor and explain its action. For example, myosin uses ATP to generate force against actin; it does not merely "recruit cellular machinery."
- Define a technical term where students first need it. An enzyme is not explained by naming several other enzymes. Introduce the relevant structure, action, and consequence in ordinary language.
- Explain intermediate steps when the sources establish them. State where a compound enters, which receptor it reaches, what the receptor changes, and how the measured response changes. Do not fill a gap in the evidence with an invented pathway.
- Use source-specific findings: which cell or animal, what treatment or manipulation, what changed, and in which direction. Explain an inhibitor by naming the step it blocks and the response that persists or disappears.
- Each paragraph adds information. Paragraph three may teach a further mechanism, a different condition, a follow-up result, or a relevant anatomical or behavioral detail. It has no fixed closing function.
- Retain a conclusion when it makes a concrete biological claim supported by the preceding evidence. Delete conclusions that merely praise the experiment, announce a connection, or say that several factors matter.
- Write connected sentences that sound natural aloud. Avoid both dense strings of unexplained terms and choppy lists of obvious facts. Do not add a fixed number of sentences.
- Preserve scientifically necessary distinctions, including hypothesis versus result, cultured cells versus intact animals, and calcium fluorescence versus transmitter release. State the distinction within the explanation rather than adding a stock caution paragraph.

Apply this deletion test to every sentence: would its removal lose a definition, mechanism, specific finding, experimental detail, or necessary scientific distinction? If not, delete or replace it. Apply the test separately to every final paragraph. Automated wording checks catch recurring failures; they do not assess scientific depth.

## Rejected wording

"The study brings drug action back to a complete causal sequence: a compound reaches a receptor, the receptor recruits intracellular signaling, effectors alter cellular function, and the changed cell contributes to a larger neural system."

This does not explain the CB1 signaling pathway, force generation, dendritic response, or the inhibitor results. Other unacceptable substitutes include "the findings place the mechanism in a broader context," "the experiment highlights the importance of cellular machinery," and "access and target location all matter."

## Instructor's preferred example

Cannabinoids can change the shape of neurons by activating CB1 receptors, which trigger signals inside the cell that affect its structure. In this study, researchers examined hippocampal neurons grown in a laboratory and observed changes in the cell body and dendrites, the branches that receive signals from other neurons. Together, these structures make up the somatodendritic region, so the findings showed that cannabinoid effects extended beyond the growing tip of the axon to other parts of the neuron.

These structural changes involve actin, a protein that forms part of the cytoskeleton, which is the internal framework that supports the cell and helps it change shape. When CB1 receptors are activated, signals inside the neuron can change how actin is organized, allowing the cell body and dendrites to change their shape. The images follow the same neuron over several minutes, allowing us to compare its appearance before and after receptor activation and see how its structure changes over time.

The length of receptor activation is important because changes in shape that happen within minutes are different from changes in growth or organization that develop after longer exposure. Researchers examined these effects separately to distinguish the neuron's immediate response from changes that emerge over time. This study shows how a chemical acting on a receptor can produce a physical change in a neuron by triggering signals that reorganize its internal framework and alter the shape of its cell body and dendrites.

Source: Roland et al. (2014), Figure 7. https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.03159.

This example is the instructor's style reference, not a requirement to use these exact sentence lengths or a template for every slide. Maintain three paragraphs and the course's rendered-line requirement. Meaningful references to a recorded change or a concrete biological conclusion are allowed; empty statements about a study's importance are not.

# Behavioral Neuroscience 392: course-specific lecture rules

These instructions apply ONLY to this course. The instructor’s request takes precedence over inherited Neuroethology rules. This is the connected BEHAVNEUR-392- GitHub repository at https://github.com/jordanxxlopez/BEHAVNEUR-392-.git. Keep all Behavioral Neuroscience materials in this repository, separate from NEUR 411.

## Deliverables and level

Build 19 chapter PowerPoints, one per verified chapter in Carlson and Birkett, Physiology of Behavior, Global Edition, 13th edition (2022), ISBN 9781292430256. Verify the table of contents before recording chapter mapping. The instructor explicitly requests descriptive lecture titles, not "Chapter 1"; use the authorized topic title in course/schedule.json. Start with Chapter 1 unless directed otherwise. Prefer 75 slides total: 1 title, 73 content, 1 final Key takeaways. Expand only when useful, to at most 85 total. Do not invent a timetable. Each chapter may span several class meetings.

This is an undergraduate Behavioral Neuroscience course, easier than NEUR 411 but intellectually demanding. Define terms at first use. Explain neuronal signaling, pathways, experimental manipulations, and behavioral findings through direct, concrete teaching sentences. Introduce unfamiliar machinery in steps; avoid graduate-level prerequisite knowledge.

## Teaching prose and transcript requirements: all chapters

Follow [course/TEACHING_STYLE.md](course/TEACHING_STYLE.md) for every chapter, every slide paragraph, and every speaker-note teaching transcript, including authorized revisions. The instructor rejected generic research-summary prose in Chapter 4 and supplied a preferred plain-language rewrite. Match that example's connected explanatory sentences, definitions woven into the prose, and clear descriptions of what changes in the cell. Teach the actual biology: identify the relevant molecule or structure, explain what it does, specify what changes, and describe the resulting cellular or behavioral response. Define unfamiliar machinery in ordinary language as it is introduced. Explain the action behind phrases such as "recruits intracellular signaling" or "changes cellular function" without replacing them with a dense chain of unexplained protein names.

Every paragraph, including paragraph three, adds substantive information from the sources. Do not close with a statement about what the study brings together, places in a broader context, illustrates, highlights, connects, or teaches. Do not replace explanation with "access, target location, and cellular machinery all matter" or another obvious list of factors. State the specific transport process, receptor location, signaling step, time-dependent change, inhibitor result, anatomy, or behavioral finding instead. A correct but empty summary is still unacceptable.

Read each slide and transcript aloud as a professor explaining the material. Sentences must develop one another, not stack unexplained technical names or repeat the title. Apply the deletion test: if a sentence can disappear without losing a definition, mechanism, source-specific finding, experimental detail, or necessary scientific distinction, remove or replace it. A plain-language conclusion is welcome when it explains the biological change, as in the instructor's supplied example. A regex pass is not a teaching-quality pass. Review the third paragraph separately for generic wrap-up language. For the current Chapter 4 revision, replace only the three content paragraphs and matching teaching transcripts. Preserve all titles, slide order, layout, figures, recordings, captions, credits, and takeaways.

## Teaching and balance

Use 30–40% textbook foundations and 60–70% primary-research teaching, adjusted to the chapter. At the preferred count, 29 foundation slides and 44 research slides give approximately 40%/60%. Foundation slides teach mechanisms from the textbook even when an existing study figure illustrates the concept; retagging alone is insufficient. Never say "the textbook" or add textbook metacommentary in visible teaching prose. References and source-image credits still identify the textbook accurately. Review every video and added image for its relationship to the adjacent concept, not merely its availability. Teach each concept, then use source-supported study findings to explain how it works. Use a manageable group of core papers across several slides rather than a different paper on every slide. Every paragraph teaches material. Use direct, concrete teaching sentences in three paragraphs. Each content paragraph must occupy 5–7 full rendered lines, checked against the exported PDF. # Behavioral Neuroscience 392: course-specific lecture rules

These instructions apply ONLY to this course. The instructor’s request takes precedence over inherited Neuroethology rules. This is the connected BEHAVNEUR-392- GitHub repository at https://github.com/jordanxxlopez/BEHAVNEUR-392-.git. Keep all Behavioral Neuroscience materials in this repository, separate from NEUR 411.

## Deliverables and level

Build 19 chapter PowerPoints, one per verified chapter in Carlson and Birkett, Physiology of Behavior, Global Edition, 13th edition (2022), ISBN 9781292430256. Verify the table of contents before recording chapter mapping. The instructor explicitly requests descriptive lecture titles, not "Chapter 1"; use the authorized topic title in course/schedule.json. Start with Chapter 1 unless directed otherwise. Prefer 75 slides total: 1 title, 73 content, 1 final Key takeaways. Expand only when useful, to at most 85 total. Do not invent a timetable. Each chapter may span several class meetings.

This is an undergraduate Behavioral Neuroscience course, easier than NEUR 411 but intellectually demanding. Define terms at first use. Explain neuronal signaling, pathways, experimental manipulations, and behavioral findings through direct, concrete teaching sentences. Introduce unfamiliar machinery in steps; avoid graduate-level prerequisite knowledge.

## Teaching prose and transcript requirements: all chapters

Follow [course/TEACHING_STYLE.md](course/TEACHING_STYLE.md) for every chapter, every slide paragraph, and every speaker-note teaching transcript, including authorized revisions. The instructor rejected generic research-summary prose in Chapter 4 and supplied a preferred plain-language rewrite. Match that example's connected explanatory sentences, definitions woven into the prose, and clear descriptions of what changes in the cell. Teach the actual biology: identify the relevant molecule or structure, explain what it does, specify what changes, and describe the resulting cellular or behavioral response. Define unfamiliar machinery in ordinary language as it is introduced. Explain the action behind phrases such as "recruits intracellular signaling" or "changes cellular function" without replacing them with a dense chain of unexplained protein names.

Every paragraph, including paragraph three, adds substantive information from the sources. Do not close with a statement about what the study brings together, places in a broader context, illustrates, highlights, connects, or teaches. Do not replace explanation with "access, target location, and cellular machinery all matter" or another obvious list of factors. State the specific transport process, receptor location, signaling step, time-dependent change, inhibitor result, anatomy, or behavioral finding instead. A correct but empty summary is still unacceptable.

Read each slide and transcript aloud as a professor explaining the material. Sentences must develop one another, not stack unexplained technical names or repeat the title. Apply the deletion test: if a sentence can disappear without losing a definition, mechanism, source-specific finding, experimental detail, or necessary scientific distinction, remove or replace it. A plain-language conclusion is welcome when it explains the biological change, as in the instructor's supplied example. A regex pass is not a teaching-quality pass. Review the third paragraph separately for generic wrap-up language. Keep this course's 5–7 rendered lines per paragraph; never import Neuroethology's older sentence quota or pad a paragraph to satisfy length. For the current Chapter 4 revision, replace only the three content paragraphs and matching teaching transcripts. Preserve all titles, slide order, layout, figures, recordings, captions, credits, and takeaways.

## Teaching and balance

Use 30–40% textbook foundations and 60–70% primary-research teaching, adjusted to the chapter. At the preferred count, 29 foundation slides and 44 research slides give approximately 40%/60%. Foundation slides teach mechanisms from the textbook even when an existing study figure illustrates the concept; retagging alone is insufficient. Tag each content slide instructional_role as foundation or research; do not count an incidental citation as research teaching. The textbook defines chapter scope and concepts. Interweave concept teaching with directly related primary studies rather than separating a foundation block from a research block. Connect studies to the topic and mechanism just introduced; emphasize current research while revisiting essential older work. Never say "the textbook" or add textbook metacommentary in visible teaching prose. References and source-image credits still identify the textbook accurately. Review every video and added image for its relationship to the adjacent concept, not merely its availability. Teach each concept, then use source-supported study findings to explain how it works. Use a manageable group of core papers across several slides rather than a different paper on every slide. Include current accessible research and foundational work where needed; verify references and quantitative claims.

Every paragraph teaches material. Use direct, concrete teaching sentences in three paragraphs. Each content paragraph must occupy 5–7 full rendered lines, checked against the exported PDF. Expand explanations rather than add filler, forced line breaks, or blank-line padding. The line requirement supersedes the earlier 70–110-word target. Identify the actor, action, and result. Do not summarize with vague verbs such as connected, linked, supported, or relationship. For example: "The neurons move the paddle. A hit or miss determines the electrical signal sent back to them." Scientific connections can still be described literally when their anatomy is the subject. Use three substantive paragraphs per content slide and natural complete-sentence teaching transcripts in notes, adapting depth to this easier class and readable layout. Do not pad paragraphs to meet a sentence count. No agendas, learning objectives, previews, fixed method-result-limitation templates, presentation commentary, or em dashes in visible text. Do not end paragraphs on routine limitations or stock caution. The instructor will discuss limitations and the importance of controls orally. Preserve scientifically necessary distinctions and genuine experimental conditions; do not turn hypotheses into facts. No p-values, error bars quoted in prose, test names, or sample-size bookkeeping. Retain quantities that explain the concept. Finish with 5–6 exam-level takeaways with bold lead phrases.

## Format

16:9, Arial throughout. Preserve the Neuroethology content-slide style. For this course’s TITLE SLIDE ONLY: white background, a large credited source image on the LEFT, and the instructor-approved descriptive lecture title, course/date, Jordan Lopez, Ph.D., and Professor of Neurobiology & Biomedical Engineering on the RIGHT. Do not mirror or recolor the source image. Body text/captions/footers black; titles and bold words use the chapter’s coordinated restrained theme. Separate theme ledger from NEUR 411; no yellow, orange, gold, purple, or green. Record themes after final validation. Never copy the former professor’s slide style. Analyze their slides for existing course coverage only when available.

## Figures

Every content slide has a relevant source image. Preserve existing intact study panels. Add a few original credited cell, anatomy, animal, or apparatus photographs where these make the slide concept recognizable. Fit images and movies without changing source aspect ratios or making scientific panels illegible. Prioritize intact primary-article panels. Textbook crops are explicitly allowed for foundations: retain original labels, caption Carlson and Birkett (2022), figure number and printed page, and record PDF page, ISBN, edition, and source. Retain enough context for students to interpret axes, labels, units, and scale bars. Never generate, redraw, replot, recolor, or reconstruct any scientific image, diagram, chart, or animation. Up to 10 genuinely useful credited web images are permitted. Give the full source reference in notes. New crops are made with tools/crop_figure.py; record crop boxes. Do not post the full uploaded textbook to GitHub.

## Videos

For Chapter 2 and subsequent new chapter decks, require exactly 20 distinct useful academic videos PLUS 20 distinct aesthetic animal/neuroscience recordings, totaling 40 embedded videos. This instructor update supersedes the former 20–30-video range. Existing Chapter 1 deliveries retain their recorded media counts unless a revision is requested. Choose each recording for its adjacent concept; do not reuse unrelated repository footage merely because it is available. For Chapter 3 onward, distribute all 40 recordings across the entire content sequence: 10 in each consecutive quarter, no gap greater than three content slides, and at least five in the final ten content slides. Never put media-purpose labels such as aesthetic, academic recording, or context video in visible slide text, captions, titles, or teaching notes. Keep these classifications only in the media manifest. Spread them through the material where appropriate; preserve article figures on video slides. Academic web/YouTube recordings by primary researchers and labs are permitted even when not publisher supplementary movies. No news reports, shorts, TikTok-style edits, unrelated entertainment, or fabricated scenes. Verify and accurately credit source authors, original URLs, study DOI when associated, and supplied license. Aesthetic recordings are real footage connected to the chapter, credited, with their purpose classified in internal records only, and never counted as primary scientific evidence or toward the academic-video quota. User uploads remain uploads, not fabricated article supplements.

Embed PowerPoint-compatible MP4s. Preserve native resolution, timing, audio, aspect ratio, and scientific scenes. Compress only when necessary and verify quality. Record video purpose (academic/aesthetic), slide, source, DOI if applicable, dimensions, duration, audio, codec, and SHA256. Verify every embedded media relationship and all source hashes; do not count duplicate excerpts as different studies or pad with repetitions. Retain static source posters. Report untested desktop playback honestly.

## Access

If a paper is blocked, find an accessible primary paper teaching the same necessary concept. Request the paper upload only if that particular source is indispensable. If a selected necessary VIDEO is blocked, stop final delivery and give an exact numbered upload list with original URL, source/paper DOI, movie identifier, and teaching purpose. Continue independent preparation. Never claim an inaccessible PDF, book, prior deck, or video was reviewed. The full book was too large to transfer, but all six split PDFs have now been downloaded. The contents and Introduction chapter were read directly; keep the full source PDFs private and ignored.

## Chapter 1 frontier section

Replace Careers in Neuroscience and Strategies for Learning with source-supported future technologies. Do not teach career advice or study strategies. Include fish-operated vehicles, the requested Winship sea-lion cursor study only after exact source verification, DeepLabCut/computer vision, wireless recordings, optogenetics with substantial stepwise coverage, and biological computing. Existing Biocomputing II and Fish-Operated Vehicle II decks are scientific/reference material, not a license to claim unverified games or capabilities. Explain the actual demonstrated task, sensory encoding, feedback, learning, and neuronal mechanism. Claims about Doom require a verified primary source documenting the actual preparation and task. Verify the 2026 Nobel award through authoritative sources before stating recipients or citation; do not infer names from classic optogenetics papers.

## Build and validation

Use tools/build_lecture.py with the verified chapter spec, then embed media and run tools/check_lecture.py and tools/check_course.py. course/policy.json records the explicit course overrides. Generic builder passes do not establish that final video quotas or 40%/60% balance are satisfied. Render all slides, inspect figures, captions, body fit, and video placement. Save the editable PPTX and a clearly labeled static PDF preview. Deliver a working direct download. Publish into BEHAVNEUR-392-; do not push course materials into the Neuroethology repository.

## Instructor-authorized Introduction history expansion

For this lecture only, 85–90 total slides are authorized. Preserve the existing 73 content slides and 30 embedded videos while reorganizing them to pair historical methods with related experiments. Add Müller, Galvani/Helmholtz, Flourens before Broca, Fritsch/Hitzig, Purkinje, the original Nobel table, and the verified 2026 optogenetics laureates with their contributions. All new paragraphs still require 5–7 actual rendered lines. Distinguish experimental ablation from clinical observation and stimulation; cardiac Purkinje fibers are specialized cardiomyocytes. The Givon vehicle study does not establish lesion effects.

## Instructor-authorized Chapter 5 expansion

For Chapter 5, the instructor requests 80–90 total slides and expanded coverage of newer methods and neuroengineering. Use 86 total slides (84 teaching slides, title, takeaways). Retain all writing, source-image, 40-video, distribution, and validation requirements above. This exception does not change other chapters' slide-count limits.

## Instructor-authorized Chapter 6 expansion

For Chapter 6, the instructor authorizes 85–90 total slides. Use 90 total slides (88 teaching slides, title, takeaways). Integrate source-supported visual illusions throughout and include a short, 3–4-slide treatment of the rewired-ferret experiments after visual cortex and receptive fields, plus relevant developmental/adult plasticity. Preserve all writing, source-image, 40-video, distribution, and validation requirements above. Revisit the ferret result briefly in the later audition lecture without repeating the full section. This exception does not change other chapters.

# Behavioral Neuroscience 392: course-specific lecture rules

These instructions apply ONLY to this course. The instructor’s request takes precedence over inherited Neuroethology rules. This is the connected BEHAVNEUR-392- GitHub repository at https://github.com/jordanxxlopez/BEHAVNEUR-392-.git. Keep all Behavioral Neuroscience materials in this repository, separate from NEUR 411.

## Deliverables and level

Build 19 chapter PowerPoints, one per verified chapter in Carlson and Birkett, Physiology of Behavior, Global Edition, 13th edition (2022), ISBN 9781292430256. Verify the table of contents before recording chapter mapping. The instructor explicitly requests descriptive lecture titles, not "Chapter 1"; use the authorized topic title in course/schedule.json. Start with Chapter 1 unless directed otherwise. Prefer 75 slides total: 1 title, 73 content, 1 final Key takeaways. Expand only when useful, to at most 85 total. Do not invent a timetable. Each chapter may span several class meetings.

This is an undergraduate Behavioral Neuroscience course, easier than NEUR 411 but intellectually demanding. Define terms at first use. Explain neuronal signaling, pathways, experimental manipulations, and behavioral findings through direct, concrete teaching sentences. Introduce unfamiliar machinery in steps; avoid graduate-level prerequisite knowledge.

## Teaching prose and transcript requirements: all chapters

Follow [course/TEACHING_STYLE.md](course/TEACHING_STYLE.md) for every chapter, every slide paragraph, and every speaker-note teaching transcript, including authorized revisions. The instructor rejected generic research-summary prose in Chapter 4 and supplied a preferred plain-language rewrite. Match that example's connected explanatory sentences, definitions woven into the prose, and clear descriptions of what changes in the cell. Teach the actual biology: identify the relevant molecule or structure, explain what it does, specify what changes, and describe the resulting cellular or behavioral response. Define unfamiliar machinery in ordinary language as it is introduced. Explain the action behind phrases such as "recruits intracellular signaling" or "changes cellular function" without replacing them with a dense chain of unexplained protein names.

Every paragraph, including paragraph three, adds substantive information from the sources. Do not close with a statement about what the study brings together, places in a broader context, illustrates, highlights, connects, or teaches. Do not replace explanation with "access, target location, and cellular machinery all matter" or another obvious list of factors. State the specific transport process, receptor location, signaling step, time-dependent change, inhibitor result, anatomy, or behavioral finding instead. A correct but empty summary is still unacceptable.

Read each slide and transcript aloud as a professor explaining the material. Sentences must develop one another, not stack unexplained technical names or repeat the title. Apply the deletion test: if a sentence can disappear without losing a definition, mechanism, source-specific finding, experimental detail, or necessary scientific distinction, remove or replace it. A plain-language conclusion is welcome when it explains the biological change, as in the instructor's supplied example. A regex pass is not a teaching-quality pass. Review the third paragraph separately for generic wrap-up language. Keep this course's 5–7 rendered lines per paragraph; never import Neuroethology's older sentence quota or pad a paragraph to satisfy length. For the current Chapter 4 revision, replace only the three content paragraphs and matching teaching transcripts. Preserve all titles, slide order, layout, figures, recordings, captions, credits, and takeaways.

## Teaching and balance

Use 30–40% textbook foundations and 60–70% primary-research teaching, adjusted to the chapter. At the preferred count, 29 foundation slides and 44 research slides give approximately 40%/60%. Foundation slides teach mechanisms from the textbook even when an existing study figure illustrates the concept; retagging alone is insufficient. Tag each content slide instructional_role as foundation or research; do not count an incidental citation as research teaching. The textbook defines chapter scope and concepts. Interweave concept teaching with directly related primary studies rather than separating a foundation block from a research block. Connect studies to the topic and mechanism just introduced; emphasize current research while revisiting essential older work. Never say "the textbook" or add textbook metacommentary in visible teaching prose. References and source-image credits still identify the textbook accurately. Review every video and added image for its relationship to the adjacent concept, not merely its availability. Teach each concept, then use source-supported study findings to explain how it works. Use a manageable group of core papers across several slides rather than a different paper on every slide. Include current accessible research and foundational work where needed; verify references and quantitative claims.

Every paragraph teaches material. Use direct, concrete teaching sentences in three paragraphs. Each content paragraph must occupy 5–7 full rendered lines, checked against the exported PDF. Expand explanations rather than add filler, forced line breaks, or blank-line padding. The line requirement supersedes the earlier 70–110-word target. Identify the actor, action, and result. Do not summarize with vague verbs such as connected, linked, supported, or relationship. For example: "The neurons move the paddle. A hit or miss determines the electrical signal sent back to them." Scientific connections can still be described literally when their anatomy is the subject. Use three substantive paragraphs per content slide and natural complete-sentence teaching transcripts in notes, adapting depth to this easier class and readable layout. Do not pad paragraphs to meet a sentence count. No agendas, learning objectives, previews, fixed method-result-limitation templates, presentation commentary, or em dashes in visible text. Do not end paragraphs on routine limitations or stock caution. The instructor will discuss limitations and the importance of controls orally. Preserve scientifically necessary distinctions and genuine experimental conditions; do not turn hypotheses into facts. No p-values, error bars quoted in prose, test names, or sample-size bookkeeping. Retain quantities that explain the concept. Finish with 5–6 exam-level takeaways with bold lead phrases.

## Format

16:9, Arial throughout. Preserve the Neuroethology content-slide style. For this course’s TITLE SLIDE ONLY: white background, a large credited source image on the LEFT, and the instructor-approved descriptive lecture title, course/date, Jordan Lopez, Ph.D., and Professor of Neurobiology & Biomedical Engineering on the RIGHT. Do not mirror or recolor the source image. Body text/captions/footers black; titles and bold words use the chapter’s coordinated restrained theme. Separate theme ledger from NEUR 411; no yellow, orange, gold, purple, or green. Record themes after final validation. Never copy the former professor’s slide style. Analyze their slides for existing course coverage only when available.

## Figures

Every content slide has a relevant source image. Preserve existing intact study panels. Add a few original credited cell, anatomy, animal, or apparatus photographs where these make the slide concept recognizable. Fit images and movies without changing source aspect ratios or making scientific panels illegible. Prioritize intact primary-article panels. Textbook crops are explicitly allowed for foundations: retain original labels, caption Carlson and Birkett (2022), figure number and printed page, and record PDF page, ISBN, edition, and source. Retain enough context for students to interpret axes, labels, units, and scale bars. Never generate, redraw, replot, recolor, or reconstruct any scientific image, diagram, chart, or animation. Up to 10 genuinely useful credited web images are permitted. Give the full source reference in notes. New crops are made with tools/crop_figure.py; record crop boxes. Do not post the full uploaded textbook to GitHub.

## Videos

For Chapter 2 and subsequent new chapter decks, require exactly 20 distinct useful academic videos PLUS 20 distinct aesthetic animal/neuroscience recordings, totaling 40 embedded videos. This instructor update supersedes the former 20–30-video range. Existing Chapter 1 deliveries retain their recorded media counts unless a revision is requested. Choose each recording for its adjacent concept; do not reuse unrelated repository footage merely because it is available. For Chapter 3 onward, distribute all 40 recordings across the entire content sequence: 10 in each consecutive quarter, no gap greater than three content slides, and at least five in the final ten content slides. Never put media-purpose labels such as aesthetic, academic recording, or context video in visible slide text, captions, titles, or teaching notes. Keep these classifications only in the media manifest. Spread them through the material where appropriate; preserve article figures on video slides. Academic web/YouTube recordings by primary researchers and labs are permitted even when not publisher supplementary movies. No news reports, shorts, TikTok-style edits, unrelated entertainment, or fabricated scenes. Verify and accurately credit source authors, original URLs, study DOI when associated, and supplied license. Aesthetic recordings are real footage connected to the chapter, credited, with their purpose classified in internal records only, and never counted as primary scientific evidence or toward the academic-video quota. User uploads remain uploads, not fabricated article supplements.

Embed PowerPoint-compatible MP4s. Preserve native resolution, timing, audio, aspect ratio, and scientific scenes. Compress only when necessary and verify quality. Record video purpose (academic/aesthetic), slide, source, DOI if applicable, dimensions, duration, audio, codec, and SHA256. Verify every embedded media relationship and all source hashes; do not count duplicate excerpts as different studies or pad with repetitions. Retain static source posters. Report untested desktop playback honestly.

# Behavioral Neuroscience 392: course-specific lecture rules

These instructions apply ONLY to this course. The instructor’s request takes precedence over inherited Neuroethology rules. This is the connected BEHAVNEUR-392- GitHub repository at https://github.com/jordanxxlopez/BEHAVNEUR-392-.git. Keep all Behavioral Neuroscience materials in this repository, separate from NEUR 411.

## Deliverables and level

Build 19 chapter PowerPoints, one per verified chapter in Carlson and Birkett, Physiology of Behavior, Global Edition, 13th edition (2022), ISBN 9781292430256. Verify the table of contents before recording chapter mapping. The instructor explicitly requests descriptive lecture titles, not "Chapter 1"; use the authorized topic title in course/schedule.json. Start with Chapter 1 unless directed otherwise. Prefer 75 slides total: 1 title, 73 content, 1 final Key takeaways. Expand only when useful, to at most 85 total. Do not invent a timetable. Each chapter may span several class meetings.

This is an undergraduate Behavioral Neuroscience course, easier than NEUR 411 but intellectually demanding. Define terms at first use. Explain neuronal signaling, pathways, experimental manipulations, and behavioral findings through direct, concrete teaching sentences. Introduce unfamiliar machinery in steps; avoid graduate-level prerequisite knowledge.

## Teaching prose and transcript requirements: all chapters

Follow [course/TEACHING_STYLE.md](course/TEACHING_STYLE.md) for every chapter, every slide paragraph, and every speaker-note teaching transcript, including authorized revisions. The instructor rejected generic research-summary prose in Chapter 4 and supplied a preferred plain-language rewrite. Match that example's connected explanatory sentences, definitions woven into the prose, and clear descriptions of what changes in the cell. Teach the actual biology: identify the relevant molecule or structure, explain what it does, specify what changes, and describe the resulting cellular or behavioral response. Define unfamiliar machinery in ordinary language as it is introduced. Explain the action behind phrases such as "recruits intracellular signaling" or "changes cellular function" without replacing them with a dense chain of unexplained protein names.

Every paragraph, including paragraph three, adds substantive information from the sources. Do not close with a statement about what the study brings together, places in a broader context, illustrates, highlights, connects, or teaches. Do not replace explanation with "access, target location, and cellular machinery all matter" or another obvious list of factors. State the specific transport process, receptor location, signaling step, time-dependent change, inhibitor result, anatomy, or behavioral finding instead. A correct but empty summary is still unacceptable.

Read each slide and transcript aloud as a professor explaining the material. Sentences must develop one another, not stack unexplained technical names or repeat the title. Apply the deletion test: if a sentence can disappear without losing a definition, mechanism, source-specific finding, experimental detail, or necessary scientific distinction, remove or replace it. A plain-language conclusion is welcome when it explains the biological change, as in the instructor's supplied example. A regex pass is not a teaching-quality pass. Review the third paragraph separately for generic wrap-up language. Keep this course's 5–7 rendered lines per paragraph; never import Neuroethology's older sentence quota or pad a paragraph to satisfy length. For the current Chapter 4 revision, replace only the three content paragraphs and matching teaching transcripts. Preserve all titles, slide order, layout, figures, recordings, captions, credits, and takeaways.

## Teaching and balance

Use 30–40% textbook foundations and 60–70% primary-research teaching, adjusted to the chapter. At the preferred count, 29 foundation slides and 44 research slides give approximately 40%/60%. Foundation slides teach mechanisms from the textbook even when an existing study figure illustrates the concept; retagging alone is insufficient. Tag each content slide instructional_role as foundation or research; do not count an incidental citation as research teaching. The textbook defines chapter scope and concepts. Interweave concept teaching with directly related primary studies rather than separating a foundation block from a research block. Connect studies to the topic and mechanism just introduced; emphasize current research while revisiting essential older work. Never say "the textbook" or add textbook metacommentary in visible teaching prose. References and source-image credits still identify the textbook accurately. Review every video and added image for its relationship to the adjacent concept, not merely its availability. Teach each concept, then use source-supported study findings to explain how it works. Use a manageable group of core papers across several slides rather than a different paper on every slide. Include current accessible research and foundational work where needed; verify references and quantitative claims.

Every paragraph teaches material. Use direct, concrete teaching sentences in three paragraphs. Each content paragraph must occupy 5–7 full rendered lines, checked against the exported PDF. Expand explanations rather than add filler, forced line breaks, or blank-line padding. The line requirement supersedes the earlier 70–110-word target. Identify the actor, action, and result. Do not summarize with vague verbs such as connected, linked, supported, or relationship. For example: "The neurons move the paddle. A hit or miss determines the electrical signal sent back to them." Scientific connections can still be described literally when their anatomy is the subject. Use three substantive paragraphs per content slide and natural complete-sentence teaching transcripts in notes, adapting depth to this easier class and readable layout. Do not pad paragraphs to meet a sentence count. No agendas, learning objectives, previews, fixed method-result-limitation templates, presentation commentary, or em dashes in visible text. Do not end paragraphs on routine limitations or stock caution. The instructor will discuss limitations and the importance of controls orally. Preserve scientifically necessary distinctions and genuine experimental conditions; do not turn hypotheses into facts. No p-values, error bars quoted in prose, test names, or sample-size bookkeeping. Retain quantities that explain the concept. Finish with 5–6 exam-level takeaways with bold lead phrases.

## Format

16:9, Arial throughout. Preserve the Neuroethology content-slide style. For this course’s TITLE SLIDE ONLY: white background, a large credited source image on the LEFT, and the instructor-approved descriptive lecture title, course/date, Jordan Lopez, Ph.D., and Professor of Neurobiology & Biomedical Engineering on the RIGHT. Do not mirror or recolor the source image. Body text/captions/footers black; titles and bold words use the chapter’s coordinated restrained theme. Separate theme ledger from NEUR 411; no yellow, orange, gold, purple, or green. Record themes after final validation. Never copy the former professor’s slide style. Analyze their slides for existing course coverage only when available.

## Figures

Every content slide has a relevant source image. Preserve existing intact study panels. Add a few original credited cell, anatomy, animal, or apparatus photographs where these make the slide concept recognizable. Fit images and movies without changing source aspect ratios or making scientific panels illegible. Prioritize intact primary-article panels. Textbook crops are explicitly allowed for foundations: retain original labels, caption Carlson and Birkett (2022), figure number and printed page, and record PDF page, ISBN, edition, and source. Retain enough context for students to interpret axes, labels, units, and scale bars. Never generate, redraw, replot, recolor, or reconstruct any scientific image, diagram, chart, or animation. Up to 10 genuinely useful credited web images are permitted. Give the full source reference in notes. New crops are made with tools/crop_figure.py; record crop boxes. Do not post the full uploaded textbook to GitHub.

## Videos

For Chapter 2 and subsequent new chapter decks, require exactly 20 distinct useful academic videos PLUS 20 distinct aesthetic animal/neuroscience recordings, totaling 40 embedded videos. This instructor update supersedes the former 20–30-video range. Existing Chapter 1 deliveries retain their recorded media counts unless a revision is requested. Choose each recording for its adjacent concept; do not reuse unrelated repository footage merely because it is available. For Chapter 3 onward, distribute all 40 recordings across the entire content sequence: 10 in each consecutive quarter, no gap greater than three content slides, and at least five in the final ten content slides. Never put media-purpose labels such as aesthetic, academic recording, or context video in visible slide text, captions, titles, or teaching notes. Keep these classifications only in the media manifest. Spread them through the material where appropriate; preserve article figures on video slides. Academic web/YouTube recordings by primary researchers and labs are permitted even when not publisher supplementary movies. No news reports, shorts, TikTok-style edits, unrelated entertainment, or fabricated scenes. Verify and accurately credit source authors, original URLs, study DOI when associated, and supplied license. Aesthetic recordings are real footage connected to the chapter, credited, with their purpose classified in internal records only, and never counted as primary scientific evidence or toward the academic-video quota. User uploads remain uploads, not fabricated article supplements.

Embed PowerPoint-compatible MP4s. Preserve native resolution, timing, audio, aspect ratio, and scientific scenes. Compress only when necessary and verify quality. Record video purpose (academic/aesthetic), slide, source, DOI if applicable, dimensions, duration, audio, codec, and SHA256. Verify every embedded media relationship and all source hashes; do not count duplicate excerpts as different studies or pad with repetitions. Retain static source posters. Report untested desktop playback honestly.

## Access

If a paper is blocked, find an accessible primary paper teaching the same necessary concept. Request the paper upload only if that particular source is indispensable. If a selected necessary VIDEO is blocked, stop final delivery and give an exact numbered upload list with original URL, source/paper DOI, movie identifier, and teaching purpose. Continue independent preparation. Never claim an inaccessible PDF, book, prior deck, or video was reviewed. The full book was too large to transfer, but all six split PDFs have now been downloaded. The contents and Introduction chapter were read directly; keep the full source PDFs private and ignored.

## Chapter 1 frontier section

Replace Careers in Neuroscience and Strategies for Learning with source-supported future technologies. Do not teach career advice or study strategies. Include fish-operated vehicles, the requested Winship sea-lion cursor study only after exact source verification, DeepLabCut/computer vision, wireless recordings, optogenetics with substantial stepwise coverage, and biological computing. Existing Biocomputing II and Fish-Operated Vehicle II decks are scientific/reference material, not a license to claim unverified games or capabilities. Explain the actual demonstrated task, sensory encoding, feedback, learning, and neuronal mechanism. Claims about Doom require a verified primary source documenting the actual preparation and task. Verify the 2026 Nobel award through authoritative sources before stating recipients or citation; do not infer names from classic optogenetics papers.

## Build and validation

Use tools/build_lecture.py with the verified chapter spec, then embed media and run tools/check_lecture.py and tools/check_course.py. course/policy.json records the explicit course overrides. Generic builder passes do not establish that final video quotas or 40%/60% balance are satisfied. Render all slides, inspect figures, captions, body fit, and video placement. Save the editable PPTX and a clearly labeled static PDF preview. Deliver a working direct download. Publish into BEHAVNEUR-392-; do not push course materials into the Neuroethology repository.

## Instructor-authorized Introduction history expansion

For this lecture only, 85–90 total slides are authorized. Preserve the existing 73 content slides and 30 embedded videos while reorganizing them to pair historical methods with related experiments. Add Müller, Galvani/Helmholtz, Flourens before Broca, Fritsch/Hitzig, Purkinje, the original Nobel table, and the verified 2026 optogenetics laureates with their contributions. All new paragraphs still require 5–7 actual rendered lines. Distinguish experimental ablation from clinical observation and stimulation; cardiac Purkinje fibers are specialized cardiomyocytes. The Givon vehicle study does not establish lesion effects.

The central deck lives in chapters/C07_Audition2 and uses internal schedule ID 702, with book chapter number 7. Include 50 distinct embedded videos, internally 25 plus 25 by the existing purpose classes, distributed 13/12/13/12 across the 98 teaching slides and at least five in the final ten. Include behavioral and cognitive neuroscience, engaging original demonstrations, music and the brain, verified USC Brain and Creativity Institute studies, and a brief relevant ferret callback. Teach brainstem and cortical processing; exclude peripheral ear anatomy, mechanics, hair-cell transduction, cochlear mechanics, and implant hardware. All original-image, explanatory three-paragraph/5–7-rendered-line, transcript, sourcing, and validation rules persist.

## Instructor preference for distinct papers across courses

Prefer primary papers, figures, and recordings that have not already appeared in the Neuroethology course. The instructor clarified this preference while requesting Chapter 9. Shared foundational concepts and the assigned chapter remain appropriate; shared papers are exceptions when a specific landmark result is difficult to replace and serves a distinct teaching purpose. Check the current Neuroethology source lists before finalizing new lecture selections and record overlaps honestly. Do not revise previously delivered lectures unless requested.

Check for previous article use across Neuroethology and this course before final selection; choose fresh papers whenever scientifically appropriate. This exception does not change other chapters.

## Instructor correction: recording-to-slide relevance

For all future media work and the current Chapter 14 revision, every recording must show a behavior, patient finding, task, anatomical structure, or physiological event actually explained on its slide. A broad connection to the chapter is insufficient, including for aesthetic recordings. For example, a vocal-tract MRI of articulation does not illustrate pure alexia, semantics, reading, or stuttering genetics. Do not repeat different utterances from the same recording collection to fill unrelated sections. Prefer directly relevant clinical patient examples, original brain recordings, and actual task demonstrations. Captions identify what is being shown, and notes state what students should observe. Review the original footage and its preparation before assigning a clip. Do not claim a clip demonstrates the adjacent paper when it comes from a different study. For the 2026-10-22 Chapter 14 correction, preserve 80 slides and 40 distinct recordings, while grouping the recordings according to their directly matching concepts; the specific placement is recorded in course/policy.json and the media alignment audit.
